items.label: 15th Plan: cut in CO2 per unit of GDP over five years
items.note: The 14th Plan's cut for the same measure was 18%. The 2025 yearly target was energy, and from 2026 it is carbon.

items.label: 2026 carbon intensity target
items.note: Replaces 2025's "energy use per unit of GDP down about 3%"

items.label: Non-fossil share of energy by 2030
items.note: 21.7% in 2025, newly in the main table

items.label: Energy intensity
items.note: The text still calls for energy use per unit of GDP to fall about 10%

footnote: Source: 15th Five-Year Plan Outline (March 2026), 14th Five-Year Plan Outline (March 2021), 2025 and 2026 Government Work Reports
notes: The point is a change of lead measure, not a brand-new constraint. Carbon intensity was already binding in the 14th Plan, with an 18% cut over five years. What changed: energy intensity left the main table and survives only in the text, which still calls for energy use per unit of GDP to fall about 10% (单位GDP能耗下降10%左右). The non-fossil share of energy use became a new binding target, 25% by 2030. The yearly target moved too: 2025 asked energy use per unit of GDP to fall about 3%, and 2026 asks CO2 per unit of GDP to fall about 3.8%. The Plan also calls for zero-carbon factories and industrial parks (建设零碳工厂和园区), and the Work Report sets up a national low-carbon transition fund. For energy-heavy plants, the account to keep is now carbon emitted, not just energy used.
